Portfolio Project Specification

WiseWallet — Smart Finance Platform

A microservices-based personal finance platform with real-time transaction processing, event-driven notifications, AI-powered financial insights, and full cloud infrastructure — covering every tool from your roadmap.

5 Microservices Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 Kafka + SQS/SNS RAG / LLM Integration Full CI/CD + Observability

01 — The Scenario

What You're Building

You're the founding backend engineer at a digital banking startup. Build the core platform from scratch — the same challenge both Wio and Mal describe in their vacancies.

🏦 Multi-Account Banking

Users create accounts (checking, savings, investment), view balances, and manage profiles. Implements Spring Security JWT auth, role-based access, and Spring Data JPA with PostgreSQL.

💸 Transaction Engine

Process deposits, withdrawals, and transfers between accounts with idempotency, balance validation, and automatic category tagging. Publishes events to Kafka for downstream consumers.

🔔 Event-Driven Notifications

Kafka consumers trigger real-time alerts: low balance warnings, large transaction notifications, daily summaries. Demonstrates fan-out via SNS/SQS pattern.

🤖 AI Financial Advisor

LLM-powered spending analysis and financial advice. Uses RAG with vector store to ground responses in the user's actual transaction history. Spring AI + pgvector.

02 — Architecture

System Design

Five services behind an API Gateway, communicating through both synchronous REST and asynchronous Kafka events. Full observability with OpenTelemetry.

Account Service

account-service · port 8081
▾

Responsibilities

  • User registration and authentication — issue JWT access + refresh tokens
  • CRUD for bank accounts (checking, savings, investment) with owner validation
  • Balance management — atomic balance updates using pessimistic locking
  • Publish account.created and account.balance-low events to Kafka

Data Model

@Entity
@Table(name = "accounts")
public class Account {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.UUID)
    private UUID id;
    private UUID userId;
    @Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)
    private AccountType type; // CHECKING, SAVINGS, INVESTMENT
    private BigDecimal balance;
    private String currency; // USD, AED, GEL
    @Version
    private Long version; // Optimistic locking
}

💸

Transaction Service

transaction-service · port 8082
▾

Responsibilities

  • Process deposits, withdrawals, and peer-to-peer transfers with idempotency keys
  • Validate balances via synchronous call to Account Service (OpenFeign client)
  • Auto-categorize transactions (groceries, utilities, entertainment) using rule engine
  • Publish txn.created and txn.categorized events to Kafka
  • Provide paginated transaction history with filters (date range, category, amount)
  • Monthly spending aggregation endpoint — consumed by AI Advisor for analysis

Key Patterns

  • DDD Layered Architecture — Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Presentation, enforced by ArchUnit
  • CQRS — separate command services (write) and query services (read), each independently testable
  • Ports & Adapters — domain repository ports are interfaces; JPA adapter classes implement them (avoids generic type conflicts with Spring Data)
  • Output port for Account Service — AccountServicePort interface in Application layer; AccountServiceAdapter (Feign) in Infrastructure
  • Transactional Outbox — DomainEventToOutboxListener writes outbox row before commit (@TransactionalEventListener), OutboxPublisherService polls every 2s
  • Transfer Saga — Reserve → Debit → Credit (6 phases), compensates via release() on any failure
  • Idempotency — IdempotencyService with REQUIRES_NEW TX; uses Java 21 sealed interface (Proceed | Cached); serialized response replay on duplicate key
  • Category Rule Engine — priority chain: TRANSFER type → MCC lookup → keyword matching → fallback OTHER; pure Java, no Spring in domain

Architecture (actual — reference for other services)

  • domain/model/ — Transaction, IdempotencyKey, OutboxEvent, enums, value objects
  • domain/repository/ — Port interfaces: TransactionRepositoryPort, IdempotencyKeyRepositoryPort, OutboxEventRepositoryPort
  • domain/event/ — Java records: TransactionCreatedDomainEvent, TransactionCategorizedDomainEvent
  • domain/exception/ — 8 domain exceptions (BusinessRuleException, SameAccountTransferException, InsufficientFundsException, …)
  • domain/service/ — CategoryRuleEngine, MccCategoryMapping, KeywordCategoryMapping (pure Java)
  • application/command/ — DepositCommandService, WithdrawalCommandService, TransferCommandService, CategoryCommandService
  • application/query/ — TransactionQueryService (readOnly = true)
  • application/port/out/ — AccountServicePort (output port interface)
  • application/shared/ — IdempotencyService
  • infrastructure/persistence/ — TransactionJpaRepository (Spring Data) + TransactionRepositoryAdapter (implements port)
  • infrastructure/client/ — AccountServiceFeignClient + AccountServiceAdapter (implements port)
  • infrastructure/messaging/ — DomainEventToOutboxListener + OutboxPublisherService
  • infrastructure/job/ — IdempotencyCleanupJob (scheduled hourly)
  • presentation/controller/ — TransactionController, CategoryController; account ownership validated from X-Account-Ids header
  • presentation/mapper/ — TransactionMapper (MapStruct)
  • presentation/exception/ — GlobalExceptionHandler handles domain exceptions + MissingRequestHeaderException

Stack

Spring Boot 3.4 Spring Data JPA OpenFeign + Resilience4j MapStruct SpringDoc OpenAPI 3 PostgreSQL 16 Liquibase Kafka Producer (idempotent, snappy) JUnit 5 + Mockito Testcontainers ArchUnit 1.3 WireMock JaCoCo 85%/75%

Notification Service

notification-service · port 8083
▾

Responsibilities

  • Consume Kafka events: txn.created, account.balance-low, alert.triggered
  • Fan-out via SNS topic → SQS queues for email, push, and webhook channels
  • Template-based notification rendering (Thymeleaf templates)
  • Notification preferences per user — opt-in/out for each channel and event type
  • Dead-letter queue (DLQ) handling for failed notification deliveries
  • Notification history API — mark as read, filter by type

Event-Driven Flow

  • Kafka consumer group → process event → publish to SNS → fan-out to SQS queues
  • Each SQS queue has a dedicated processor (email worker, webhook worker)
  • Retry with exponential backoff → DLQ after 3 failures

Stack

Kafka Consumer AWS SNS AWS SQS Spring Boot 3 PostgreSQL JUnit 5

AI Advisor Service

advisor-service · port 8084
▾

Responsibilities

  • Generate AI-powered spending insights: "You spent 40% more on dining this month"

05 — Build Order

Step-by-Step Implementation

Aligned with your 4-week roadmap. Each step builds on the previous one — you have a working, progressively richer system at every stage.

Project Skeleton & Account Service CRUD WEEK 1

Create a multi-module Gradle project via Spring Initializr. Build the Account Service first — User entity, Account entity, JPA repositories, REST controllers. Get a clean CRUD API running with PostgreSQL in Docker Compose. Write your first JUnit 5 + Mockito tests.

Authentication & API Gateway WEEK 1

Add Spring Security with JWT to Account Service (issue tokens on login). Stand up API Gateway with Spring Cloud Gateway — route /api/accounts/** to Account Service. Add JWT validation filter in the Gateway. Test with Postman or HTTPie.

Transaction Service & Inter-Service Communication WEEK 2

Build Transaction Service — deposit, withdraw, transfer endpoints. Use OpenFeign to call Account Service for balance validation. Implement the saga pattern for transfers (debit → credit → compensating rollback). Add idempotency key handling. Write integration tests with Testcontainers.

Kafka Integration & Event Publishing WEEK 2

Add Kafka to Docker Compose. Configure Spring Kafka in Transaction Service — publish txn.created events on every transaction. Implement the transactional outbox pattern (write event to DB → poll and publish). Add Kafka consumer in Account Service for cross-service balance sync.

Notification Service & SNS/SQS Fan-Out WEEK 3

Build Notification Service — Kafka consumer listens for events. Implement SNS/SQS pattern using LocalStack in Docker for local development. Set up DLQ for failed deliveries. Add notification preferences and history endpoints. Wire through Gateway.

Terraform & Docker Deployment WEEK 3

Write Dockerfiles for each service (multi-stage builds with JVM tuning). Create Terraform configs: VPC, ECS Fargate cluster, RDS PostgreSQL, ElastiCache Redis, MSK (managed Kafka). Define everything in /infra directory. Test with terraform plan against AWS free tier.

CI/CD Pipeline & Deployment Strategy WEEK 3

GitHub Actions workflow: checkout → build → test → Docker build → push to ECR → deploy to ECS. Add test coverage gates (JaCoCo). Implement blue/green deployment with ECS task definitions. Add a feature flag for the AI Advisor endpoint.

Observability Stack WEEK 4

Add OpenTelemetry Java agent to all services (auto-instrumentation). Configure Micrometer metrics → Prometheus. Set up Grafana dashboards for request latency, error rates, Kafka lag. Add structured JSON logging with Logback + correlation IDs. Spring Boot Actuator health endpoints.

AI Advisor Service & RAG Pipeline WEEK 4

Build AI Advisor — consumes txn.categorized events, aggregates monthly spending, embeds summaries into pgvector. Implement RAG: on user query, embed question → similarity search → inject context → LLM call via Spring AI ChatClient. Add session-based conversation memory. This is your "wow factor" feature.

Resilience, Polish & Documentation WEEK 4

Add Resilience4j circuit breakers to all inter-service calls (fallback responses). Rate limiting on Gateway with Redis. Write a comprehensive README.md with architecture diagram, setup instructions, and design decisions. Record a 3-minute demo video walking through the system.

07 — Service Architecture Blueprint

The Pattern Every Service Should Follow

The Transaction Service is fully implemented and acts as the reference architecture. All subsequent services (Account, Notification, AI Advisor) must follow the same DDD Layered structure, CQRS split, port/adapter pattern, and ArchUnit enforcement.

Four-Layer Package Structure

Domain
Pure Java — zero framework imports. model/ (JPA entities, enums, value objects) · repository/ (port interfaces — no JPA annotations) · event/ (Java records) · exception/ (domain exceptions extend RuntimeException) · service/ (domain services — constructible without Spring context)
Dependency rule: may not import any other layer
Application
Use case orchestrators — CQRS split required. command/ (write: @Transactional, publishes ApplicationEvents) · query/ (read: @Transactional(readOnly=true), no side effects) · port/out/ (output port interfaces for external services) · shared/ (cross-cutting application services, e.g. IdempotencyService)
Dependency rule: may only access Domain + Presentation (for DTOs/mapper injection)
Infrastructure
Framework implementations of domain/application ports. persistence/ (JpaRepository interfaces + *RepositoryAdapter classes) · client/ (FeignClient + *Adapter implements output port) · messaging/ (domain event listener, outbox poller, Kafka producers/consumers) · config/ (Spring @Configuration beans, filters) · job/ (@Scheduled background jobs)
Dependency rule: may only access Domain + Application
Presentation
HTTP boundary — controllers, DTOs, mappers, exception handling. controller/ (@RestController — validates headers, routes to command/query services) · dto/request/, dto/response/ (Java records with @Valid annotations) · mapper/ (MapStruct @Mapper(componentModel="spring")) · exception/ (@RestControllerAdvice maps domain exceptions → HTTP codes)
Dependency rule: may only access Application + Domain

Key Patterns (Apply to Every Service)

🔌 JPA Repository Adapter Pattern

Never make a JPA Spring Data interface implement a domain port — generic type conflicts will occur. Always create a dedicated *RepositoryAdapter class annotated with @Repository that wraps the JPA interface and delegates all calls.

// Domain layer — interface, no JPA
public interface XxxRepositoryPort {
    Xxx save(Xxx entity);
    Optional<Xxx> findById(UUID id);
}

// Infrastructure — Spring Data (pure)
public interface XxxJpaRepository
    extends JpaRepository<Xxx, UUID> {}

// Infrastructure — adapter bridges the two
@Repository
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class XxxRepositoryAdapter
    implements XxxRepositoryPort {

    private final XxxJpaRepository jpa;

    public Xxx save(Xxx e) { return jpa.save(e); }
    public Optional<Xxx> findById(UUID id) { return jpa.findById(id); }
}

📤 Domain Events + Outbox Listener

Command services publish domain events (Java records in domain/event/) via Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher. Infrastructure listens with @TransactionalEventListener(phase = BEFORE_COMMIT) to write an outbox row atomically. A @Scheduled poller publishes to Kafka.

// domain/event — pure Java record
public record XxxCreatedDomainEvent(Xxx entity) {}

// application/command — publishes inside @Transactional
eventPublisher.publishEvent(new XxxCreatedDomainEvent(entity));

// infrastructure/messaging — writes outbox row, SAME TX
@TransactionalEventListener(phase = BEFORE_COMMIT)
public void handle(XxxCreatedDomainEvent e) {
    outboxRepo.save(buildEvent(e.entity(), "xxx.created"));
}

🔁 External Service Output Port

Dependency on an external service is represented as a port interface in application/port/out/. Application command services depend only on the interface. Infrastructure provides the Feign-based adapter. This makes command services fully unit-testable with a mock.

// application/port/out — interface
public interface OtherServicePort {
    void doAction(UUID id, BigDecimal amount);
}

// infrastructure/client — Feign adapter
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class OtherServiceAdapter
    implements OtherServicePort {

    private final OtherServiceFeignClient feign;
    public void doAction(UUID id, BigDecimal a) {
        feign.doAction(id, new ActionRequest(a));
    }
}

🏛️ ArchUnit Enforcement

Every service must include an arch/ArchitectureTest.java that verifies the layer dependency rules at build time. Use consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers() to avoid false positives from third-party libraries.

@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "com.wisewallet.xxx",
    importOptions = DoNotIncludeTests.class)
public class ArchitectureTest {

    @ArchTest
    static final ArchRule layeringRule =
        layeredArchitecture()
        .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
        .layer("Domain").definedBy("..domain..")
        .layer("Application").definedBy("..application..")
        .layer("Infrastructure").definedBy("..infrastructure..")
        .layer("Presentation").definedBy("..presentation..")
        .whereLayer("Domain").mayNotAccessAnyLayer()
        .whereLayer("Application")
            .mayOnlyAccessLayers("Domain", "Presentation")
        .whereLayer("Infrastructure")
            .mayOnlyAccessLayers("Domain", "Application")
        .whereLayer("Presentation")
            .mayOnlyAccessLayers("Application", "Domain");
}

Auth & Headers Convention

No service implements Spring Security. Auth is delegated to the API Gateway, which validates JWTs and injects user context as HTTP headers. Every service trusts these headers as the source of truth for identity and ownership.

HeaderTypeInjected byPurpose
X-User-IdUUIDAPI GatewayAuthenticated user's ID — stored on every entity
X-Account-IdsCSV of UUIDsAPI GatewayAccounts owned by the user — controllers validate accountId against this list
Idempotency-KeyString (max 255)ClientClient-supplied deduplication key — required on all write endpoints
X-Correlation-IDUUID stringCorrelationIdFilterPropagated or generated per request, set in MDC for log correlation

Global Exception Handling Convention

Every service's GlobalExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice) must handle these mappings consistently:

ExceptionHTTP Status
MethodArgumentNotValidException400 — body includes per-field validation errors
MissingRequestHeaderException400 — missing required header name in message
ConstraintViolationException400 — constraint violations list
*NotFoundException404
BusinessRuleException (and subclasses)422 Unprocessable Entity
DuplicateKeyException / conflict types409 Conflict
ResponseStatusExceptionstatus from exception (e.g. 403 for ownership violation)
*ServiceUnavailableException503
Exception (fallback)500 — logged with full stack trace

08 — Local Setup

Docker Compose Blueprint

Everything runs locally with a single docker compose up. Use LocalStack for AWS services.

# docker-compose.yml (infrastructure services)
services:
  postgres:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    ports: ["5432:5432"]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: wisewallet
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev_password
    volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports: ["6379:6379"]

  kafka:
    image: confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.6.0
    ports: ["9092:9092"]
    environment:
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@kafka:29093
      # ... KRaft mode config (no Zookeeper)

  localstack:
    image: localstack/localstack:latest
    ports: ["4566:4566"]
    environment:
      SERVICES: sns,sqs
      # Simulates AWS SNS/SQS locally

  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    ports: ["9090:9090"]
    volumes: [./infra/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml]

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    ports: ["3000:3000"]

volumes:
  pgdata:
The point of this project isn't to ship a production banking app — it's to demonstrate, in a single GitHub repo, that you can architect, build, test, deploy, and observe a modern Java microservices system with all the tools both Wio and Mal expect. When an interviewer asks "tell me about a distributed system you've built," this is your answer.
